messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• Urban roads: 25–45 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph during school hours. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must use a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles on the right yield to those on the left. | | **Headlights** | • Must be used from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Toll Roads** | • Texas has electronic toll collection (TxTag).
• Toll rates vary by lane and time of day. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 15 ft of a fire hydrant.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspections are mandatory in most counties. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not exceed speed limit when overtaking. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing. | | **Roadside Assistance** | • Texas DOT provides roadside assistance for registered vehicles. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1) – full statutory text. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) website – regulations, forms, and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement guidelines and public safety notices. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Speed cameras in high‑risk areas. - Random breath‑testing checkpoints. - Seat‑belt enforcement campaigns during holiday weekends. If you need specific statutes, detailed regulations, or recent changes, let me know!
